]

THE COURT:
For
the sake of expediency, I am delivering these reasons orally. When I refer to
the need for expediency, the underlying application in this matter is scheduled
to proceed on March 4, 2025, for three days. In this application, the
applicant seeks intervenor status on the application that is proceeding next
week.

[
2
]

For context, the plaintiff's claim is in
defamation. It relates to events at the University of British Columbia touching
on the current conflict in Gaza. Within the plaintiff's defamation action, the
defendants have filed an application to dismiss the action under the provisions
of the
Protection of Public Participation Act
,
S.B.C. 2019, c. 3 [PPPA].
As noted, the applicant here seeks to intervene in that application. This
application is made by a group called the Jewish Faculty Network (“JFN”).

[
3
]

All parties agree that an application of this
sort invokes the exercise of my discretion.

[
4
]

In this application, I am exercising my
discretion against allowing the JFN to have intervenor status on the “SLAPP”
application that is coming up next week.

[
5
]

I have various reasons for making this decision.

[
6
]

The first reason is the late nature of the
application. The application materials from the parties are already filed. By
definition, if intervenor status were granted, new arguments would be put
forward by the intervenor, requiring the defendants to answer those arguments
in time for the hearing next week. In my opinion, that is inappropriate.

[
7
]

Further, at the time this application was made
on behalf of JFN, the proposed intervenor was represented by the same law firm
as the plaintiff. I was later informed that that firm had indicated to JFN that
it would not be acting for them (should intervenor status be granted). However,
in my opinion, that scenario raises a significant concern that the submission
of the intervenor does not represent a unique and independent prospective, but
it is, in fact, simply a repetition of the plaintiff's position in the guise of
an argument in the public interest.

[
8
]

Further, I have concern about the nature of the
representative position of the spokesperson for JFN. JFN is not a legal entity.
I was not taken to any document indicating a governing structure of that
organization. The person who swore an affidavit in support of this application
is certainly a member of JFN, but I have no information to confirm whether that
person's views are prevailing views among the organization.

[
9
]

Still further, in my opinion, granting
intervenor status in an application under the
PPPA
should be a rare
event. The
PPPA

was introduced in order to facilitate a quick and efficient
resolution to actions known as SLAPP litigation. In my opinion, it is
antithetical to the quick resolution of those actions for the defendants to
have to deal with this sort of application or to deal with intervenors in
general.

[
10
]

Finally, in my opinion, the intervention of JFN would not assist the
judge deciding the SLAPP application. I have heard from counsel for JFN that
JFN would be providing information regarding academic independence and freedom
on university campuses. In my opinion, that will not be helpful for the judge
making the decision.

[
11
]

So, for all the reasons set out above, I dismiss the application for
intervenor status.

[
12
]

I am not inclined to grant costs to any party.

[
13
]

That ends my reasons.

“A. Ross J.”
